bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Macroeconomic and geopolitical instability across global operations — Geopolitical instability and volatility in the global economy may pose risks such as foreign exchange risk to the Company's global operations. Mitigation rests on operations, sales and supply sources diversified across multiple geographies and business segments plus an extensive global vendor network.
- Raw material price volatility and supply-chain disruption — Disruptions in the supply chain may lead to fluctuations in key raw material prices such as fibre, cement, resin and wood, adversely affecting operating costs and margins. Long-term partnerships with key suppliers and a diversified global supplier network are the stated mitigants.
- Technology obsolescence and cybersecurity — Failure to adopt evolving technologies may hurt operational efficiency and customer experience, while data breaches or unauthorised access could cause operational disruption and reputational damage. The Company points to advanced infrastructure at manufacturing facilities, significant investment in digitalisation and periodic IT general control and cybersecurity reviews.
- Product quality and certification compliance — Failure to maintain product quality and comply with applicable quality standards may adversely affect reputation and financial performance - material in a branded building-products business. Stringent quality control processes and accreditation by leading industry bodies for product certification are the stated controls.
- Human capital attrition and leadership retention — Because BirlaNu holds leadership positions across several product segments, its workforce attracts interest from competitors seeking experienced talent. Mitigation is through adequately staffed critical positions, structured succession planning, leadership and individual development programmes, academic partnerships and employer branding.
- Health and safety across manufacturing operations — Failure to maintain adequate health and safety standards could create an adverse working environment and affect operational continuity. The Company runs a comprehensive Environment, Health and Safety framework, structured safety processes, regular training, periodic health check-ups and ISO-certified occupational health and safety management systems across plants.
- Climate change and extreme weather disruption — Extreme weather events including heavy rainfall pose operational risks across business segments. Manufacturing facilities are supported by infrastructure designed to address climate-related risks, backed by a Business Continuity Plan with disaster recovery provisions.
- Environmental compliance and licence to operate — Growing emphasis on environmental protection raises the bar on responsible practices; failure to adequately protect the environment may adversely affect reputation and long-term sustainability. Structured environmental management programmes are in place across operations.
- Foreign exchange exposure and acquisition integration — Global operations expose the Company to currency fluctuations that may adversely affect profitability, and international operations and acquisitions may influence operating costs and revenue generation. Forward contracts hedge currency risk and a structured integration framework is used for acquisitions.

business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

business.body:
- [Rebranding] "HIL is now BirlaNu" - the company was renamed from HIL Limited to BirlaNu Limited, with "Nu" standing for "reinvention and fresh perspectives"; the change journey is presented as a full brand-architecture unification across categories.
- [Acquisition] Clean Coats Private Limited was acquired in the 2025-2026 period and now appears as a brand, "BirlaNu Clean Coats".
- [Digital/AI] "Commenced implementation of our enterprise-wide AI roadmap across commercial use cases", with expanded data lakes, AI-backed demand planning analytics, Industry 4.0 deployment across manufacturing, AI-enabled WhatsApp and voice-based customer engagement, and ISO/IEC 27001:2022 recertification achieved.
- [Europe demand] Parador faced a "Middle East crisis-induced European demand slump"; the deck states revenues were "at par with last year's levels" and "Order book is up 10% over LY, signaling a strong H2 recovery".

business.body: BirlaNu makes and sells sustainable home and building solutions for homeowners, builders and designers, with a portfolio covering pipes, construction chemicals, putty, roofs, walls and floors under brands such as BirlaNu Leakproof Pipes, Topline, BirlaNu Construction Chemicals, BirlaNu TruColour Putty, Charminar, BirlaNu Aerocon, Clean Coats and Parador. Founded in 1946 as Hyderabad Asbestos Cement Products Ltd and later renamed Hyderabad Industries and then HIL, the company rebranded to BirlaNu in FY25, unifying all product categories under one identity. Its products go into commercial, healthcare, hospitality, residential and infrastructure projects worldwide, supported by innovation centres in India and Germany and a global channel network.

outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

outlook.body:
- Complete the HIL-to-BirlaNu transition and run a unified brand proposition, bringing Pipes, Construction Chemicals, Putty, Roofs, Walls and Floors under one identity across consumer, channel and influencer networks
- Strategic portfolio rebalancing towards high-growth, higher-margin categories, demonstrated by the Clean Coats acquisition and the new Andhra Pradesh Boards plant
- Aggressive scale-up of Construction Chemicals, with Clean Coats described as the first of multiple initiatives in the segment
- Pipes acceleration: unlocking volume pathways through a sales acceleration programme and multi-segment portfolio expansion
- Walls premiumisation: expanding capacities and shifting mix toward premium tiers, anchored by the greenfield investment in Nellore
- Parador scale-up: geographic and channel expansion across Europe and the U.S. to harvest international investments
- Structural profitability: embedding margin resilience company-wide, with the Optimus value-enhancement programme's full fiscal benefits expected in FY27
- Innovation-led premiumisation: upgrading mix through FY26 rollouts including OPVC and OBS lines in Pipes and next-generation Construction Chemical formulations
- Stated ambition to double the portfolio over the next few years while reshaping it towards value-added and differentiated offerings
- Embedding AI and advanced digital capabilities across sales, manufacturing, supply chain and customer touchpoints to convert operational data into actionable intelligence
- Agile cost management through structural value-enhancement exercises across key product segments
- Investing in leadership development, capability building and a culture of agility, collaboration and continuous learning
- The stated philosophy is continuous reinvestment for growth and expansion of the business, combining organic capacity build-out with targeted acquisitions - the Clean Coats acquisition is cited as strengthening the Company's position in specialty coatings. Alongside growth spending, management emphasises protecting returns through cost and profitability management: improved contribution margins driven by lower raw material and freight costs, sourcing excellence, and efficient management of working capital and inventory to limit the impact of headwinds. Input-cost exposure is managed by building long-term supplier partnerships and a mapped, diversified global vendor base that insulates the Company from geopolitical instability and keeps logistics moving. The Company also plans to extend AI and advanced analytics to enterprise-level procurement, intelligent supply chain optimisation and smart decision-support systems to unlock further value. Executive pay is explicitly outcome-linked, with performance-linked variable pay and a Long-term Cash Incentive Plan 2025 tied to Company performance and NRC/Board-agreed targets; management notes profits in FY2026-27 may be inadequate against Section 197 limits, in which case remuneration would be paid as minimum remuneration under Schedule V. Governance oversight of these choices sits with the Audit Committee (financial reporting and internal controls), the Risk Management Committee and the Nomination and Remuneration cum Compensation Committee.
- Structured environmental management programmes across operations focused on optimising energy consumption, maintaining a balanced ecological footprint and supporting the objective of zero effluents and emissions
- Investment in ISO-certified occupational health and safety (OH&S) management systems across manufacturing plants, within a comprehensive Environment, Health and Safety (EHS) framework
- Structured safety processes, regular training programmes and periodic employee health check-ups implemented across facilities, with infrastructure and systems aimed at an incident-free workplace
- Business Continuity Plan including disaster recovery provisions to address climate-related and other operational disruptions
- Whistle-blower policy offering complete confidentiality and protection against harassment or retaliation, with a zero-tolerance approach to reported ethical breaches
- Risk governance architecture: a board-adopted risk management policy implemented under the Risk Management Committee, with the Audit Committee supervising identification, assessment and monitoring of key risks
- Internal financial controls framework with control self-assessment by process owners, independent evaluation by audit partners and Ernst & Young continuing as Internal Audit partner; the Company intends to strengthen analytics-driven audits, selective automation and governance/risk/compliance awareness through structured training and workshops
- Skilling and certification programmes for tradespeople such as plumbers, masons, applicators and painters, plus the iSAIL Sales Learning Academy and competency-based assessments for campus hires and apprentices
- Detailed environmental disclosures are stated to be available in the Company's Business Responsibility & Sustainability Report, which is not included in the routed text
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: The routed capex sections of the annual report describe expansion mainly in narrative terms rather than as a project-wise capex plan. During FY26 the Company added new capacities and introduced new products, and states that with these additions it anticipates positive growth momentum in the coming year. At a standalone level borrowings increased marginally despite additional borrowings taken towards the acquisition of Clean Coats and capex for capacity enhancement, with the increase contained by efficient working capital management. The other expansion event of the year was inorganic: the Board approved and the Company completed the acquisition of 100% of the paid-up equity share capital of Clean Coats Private Limited on November 11, 2025 under a Share Purchase Agreement, making Clean Coats a wholly owned subsidiary and strengthening the construction chemicals business. No commissioning dates, project capex amounts or plant-wise capacity figures for new projects are disclosed in the routed text.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Management enters FY27 with a stance of measured optimism, citing brand strength, structural portfolio diversity and execution agility against persisting geopolitical and macroeconomic challenges
- H2 FY26 margin performance was lifted by structural value-enhancement exercises, and the full fiscal benefits of the Optimus programme are expected to be visible in FY27
- Walls demand was propelled by volume expansion in Boards and Panels; capacity expansion and premium mix shift are the stated levers ahead
- Construction Chemicals is the youngest and fastest-scaling vertical; integrating Clean Coats expands the value-added solution suite
- Roofs leadership is being sustained through strict pricing discipline, a premium over the broader market and continuous innovation
- Pipes was hit by delayed government spending on water infrastructure, slower execution and plunging resin prices; margin recovery came from a targeted sales acceleration programme and operational efficiencies
- Parador momentum is expected to return via deeper European retail penetration, U.S. and India market expansion, targeted pricing corrections and the full annualised benefits of FY26 cost optimisations
- Fibre cement roofing demand is supported by resilient rural demand, replacement-led offtake and a higher Ministry of Rural Development budget allocation, with the widening price gap versus steel roofing sheets strengthening its value proposition
- The Indian plastic pipes industry is expected to grow only in low single digits in volume terms over FY27 and the medium term, constrained by slow public water-infrastructure spending, fragmentation and over-capacity
- PVC and CPVC prices are likely to stay soft and volatile on weak global demand and the government's evolving stance on anti-dumping protection, creating uncertainty around margins, channel behaviour and offtake
- The European flooring outlook is guarded and expected to remain flat at best, with the recovery cycle possibly deferred by a few quarters on Middle East-driven energy, freight and inflation uncertainty
- Indian macro backdrop: sustained public infrastructure capex and real estate momentum support building-materials demand, offset by weak monsoon projections, input cost inflation and new wage-code transition costs
outlook.title: Demand & outlook drivers

deepdive.thesis: BirlaNu delivered strong Q4 margin expansion (380bps standalone EBITDA) driven by cost discipline and Clean Coats integration, with Pipes segment rebounding sharply on resin price volatility; the company is now positioned for sustained profitability growth in FY27 through portfolio mix shift toward high-margin Construction Chemicals and Walls, supported by new capacity and operational efficiencies.
